Rate functions

Source: R/rate_functions.R
rate_funcs.Rd

Functions that map animation progress t in [0, 1] to an eased value. Pass one as rate_func to any animation or to Scene$play(). Manim's smooth is called smooth_rate so it does not mask stats::smooth().

Usage

linear(t, ...)

smooth_rate(t, ...)

smoothstep(t, ...)

smootherstep(t, ...)

smoothererstep(t, ...)

rush_into(t, ...)

rush_from(t, ...)

slow_into(t, ...)

double_smooth(t, ...)

there_and_back(t, ...)

there_and_back_with_pause(t, ...)

running_start(t, ...)

not_quite_there(func = smooth_rate, proportion = 0.7)

wiggle(t, ...)

squish_rate_func(func, a = 0.4, b = 0.6)

lingering(t, ...)

exponential_decay(t, ...)

ease_in_sine(t, ...)

ease_out_sine(t, ...)

ease_in_out_sine(t, ...)

ease_in_quad(t, ...)

ease_out_quad(t, ...)

ease_in_out_quad(t, ...)

ease_in_cubic(t, ...)

ease_out_cubic(t, ...)

ease_in_out_cubic(t, ...)

ease_in_quart(t, ...)

ease_out_quart(t, ...)

ease_in_out_quart(t, ...)

ease_in_quint(t, ...)

ease_out_quint(t, ...)

ease_in_out_quint(t, ...)

ease_in_expo(t, ...)

ease_out_expo(t, ...)

ease_in_out_expo(t, ...)

ease_in_circ(t, ...)

ease_out_circ(t, ...)

ease_in_out_circ(t, ...)

ease_in_back(t, ...)

ease_out_back(t, ...)

ease_in_out_back(t, ...)

ease_in_elastic(t, ...)

ease_out_elastic(t, ...)

ease_in_out_elastic(t, ...)

ease_out_bounce(t, ...)

ease_in_bounce(t, ...)

ease_in_out_bounce(t, ...)

Arguments

t

Progress between 0 and 1.

...

Optional shape parameters of some rate functions: inflection, the steepness of the sigmoid (smooth_rate(), rush_into(), rush_from(), there_and_back(); default 10); pause_ratio, the fraction of the time spent paused at the peak (there_and_back_with_pause(); default 1/3); pull_factor, how far to pull back before starting (running_start(); default -0.5); wiggles, the number of wiggles (wiggle(); default 2); and half_life, the half life of the decay (exponential_decay(); default 0.1). Other rate functions take none.

func

A rate function.

proportion

Final proportion reached.

a, b

Interval to squish the rate function into.

Value

A rate function returns a number: the progress of an animation at the proportion t of its run time. The functions that take a rate function return a new rate function.

Examples

smooth_rate(0.5)
#> [1] 0.5
there_and_back(0.25)
#> [1] 0.5
